description: Detects curl invocations carrying Content-Type application/x-sentry-envelope, which the malicious onering 1.4.1 build script uses to disguise stolen git diffs as Sentry crash telemetry.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-rust-crate-onering-performs-code-exfiltration
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.exfiltration
  - attack.t1041
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_curl:
    Image|endswith: '\curl.exe'
  selection_header:
    CommandLine|contains: 'x-sentry-envelope'
  condition: selection_curl and selection_header
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate Sentry CLI integrations that use curl directly (extremely rare — the official sentry-cli uses its own HTTP client)
level: critical
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:*\curl.exe OR @Image:*\CURL.EXE OR @Image:*\Curl.exe) @CommandLine:(*x-sentry-envelope* OR *"/envelope/"*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\curl(\.exe)?$/i
| regex("x-sentry-envelope|/envelope/", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="curl.exe" OR Processes.process_name="curl") Processes.process="*x-sentry-envelope*" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="curl.exe" OR Processes.process_name="curl") Processes.process="*x-sentry-envelope*" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock pinning compromised onering 1.4.1 AIDelivery High
The root cause is dependency resolution to onering version 1.4.1. Detecting file writes or process command lines that introduce this specific version into a manifest catches the supply-chain compromise before the build runs. Rationale: Article's sole IOC version is onering 1.4.1 from crates.io and the maintainer's GitHub. Matching cargo add/install/update for the literal 'onering' token and watching Cargo manifest mutations catches the dependency-introduction step before build.rs executes. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1
ATT&CKT1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate use of onering pre-compromise (versions before 1.4.1) — refine with version pin extraction
  • Internal forks or mirrors of the crate
  • Cargo.lock auto-updates during routine cargo update sweeps
  • CI dependency-bot PRs (Dependabot/Renovate)
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "1.3." and ProcessCommandLine !has "1.2."
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: extract the pinned version from Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock; only 1.4.1 (and any version >= 1.4.1 if maintainer pushed follow-ups) is malicious. Step 2 — Contain: pin to the last known-good version (< 1.4.1) and force a `cargo clean && cargo build` to invalidate the cached build script binary; revoke any secrets from commits made while 1.4.1 was building. Step 3 — Hunt: sweep every developer/CI repo's Cargo.lock for the string `onering` and version `1.4.1`; cross-check the maintainer's GitHub fork too since the article notes the git source is also compromised.
let FileWrites = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName in~ ("Cargo.toml","Cargo.lock")
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let ProcessCmds = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "onering"
    | where FileName in~ ("cargo.exe","cargo")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("add","install","update")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ProcessCommandLine, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath;
union FileWrites, ProcessCmds
| order by Timestamp desc
let FileWrites = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where TargetFileName in~ ("Cargo.toml","Cargo.lock")
    | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine;
let ProcessCmds = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where (ActingProcessCommandLine has "onering" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "onering")
    | where ActingProcessName =~ "cargo.exe" or ActingProcessName =~ "cargo" or TargetProcessName =~ "cargo.exe"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("add","install","update") or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("add","install","update")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername;
union FileWrites, ProcessCmds
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Cargo Manifest References Compromised onering 1.4.1 Crate
id: 3b9e7c1a-6f24-4d83-92b1-8a0d1e2f3b05
description: Detects Cargo add/install/update commands referencing the compromised onering crate (version 1.4.1 known malicious) used to pull the supply-chain payload.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-rust-crate-onering-performs-code-exfiltration
  - https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_cargo:
    Image|endswith: '\cargo.exe'
  selection_action:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' add '
      - ' install '
      - ' update '
  selection_target:
    CommandLine|contains: 'onering'
  condition: selection_cargo and selection_action and selection_target
falsepositives:
  - Internal mirror references to an unrelated 'onering' crate (none currently known)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:*\cargo.exe OR @Image:*\Cargo.exe OR @Image:*\CARGO.EXE) @CommandLine:(*onering* AND (*" add "* OR *" install "* OR *" update "*))
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\cargo(\.exe)?$/i regex("\b(add|install|update)\b.*onering", field=CommandLine))
OR
(#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/(Cargo\.toml|Cargo\.lock)$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as path from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="Cargo.toml" OR Filesystem.file_name="Cargo.lock") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | join type=outer dest [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*cargo add onering*" OR Processes.process="*cargo install onering*") by Processes.dest Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`] | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as path from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="Cargo.toml" OR Filesystem.file_name="Cargo.lock") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | join type=outer dest [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*cargo add onering*" OR Processes.process="*cargo install onering*") by Processes.dest Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`] | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Sentry envelope POST payload pattern in proxy / HTTP capture AICommand & Control Medium
If proxy / network capture is available, the onering exfiltration packet is a Sentry envelope POST containing a 'patch' field inside extra. Pattern-match on the envelope shape posted to non-corporate Sentry tenants. Rationale: Article shows the literal envelope payload structure: a JSON line with type:event, message 'on build', level:info, platform:rust, and an extra.patch field. Tying outbound POSTs to Sentry ingest endpoints originating from build tooling (curl/cargo/rustc) — and excluding actual Sentry SDK user agents — surfaces this exfil shape even without the specific DSN.
ATT&CKT1567 T1041
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal Sentry self-host instances on non-Sentry domains (excluded by domain filter)
  • Sentry SDK in a Rust application legitimately reporting crashes (UA filter)
  • Sentry CLI tool uploads
  • Developer testing Sentry integrations
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm the destination DSN (org/project IDs in the URL path) matches the onering IOC or another unknown tenant. Step 2 — Contain: block the Sentry ingest subdomain at proxy/firewall for non-approved tenants, kill the originating build. Step 3 — Hunt: pull payload captures if proxy supports it; look for 'extra.patch' or 'on build' message string. Inventory every Cargo.lock for onering.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has ".ingest." and RemoteUrl has ".sentry.io"
| where RemoteUrl has "/envelope/"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("sentry-cli.exe","node.exe","python.exe","java.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("cargo.exe","rustc.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName startswith "build-script-build"
   or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "curl.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)\.ingest\..*sentry\.io.*\/envelope\/"
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !startswith "sentry."
   and HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !startswith "sentry-"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpMethod, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpResponseHeaderContentType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd OR source:zeek) @http.method:POST @http.url:(*.ingest.*sentry.io*envelope*) -@http.useragent:(sentry.* OR sentry-*)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/\.ingest\..*sentry\.io$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4}, field=aid, include=[ContextImageFileName, RemotePort])
| ContextImageFileName=/(curl|cargo|rustc|build-script-build|sh|bash|pwsh|powershell)/i
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as url from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method="POST" Web.url="*ingest*sentry.io*envelope*" (Web.http_content_type="application/x-sentry-envelope" OR Web.http_user_agent!="sentry*") NOT Web.dest_domain IN ("sentry.your-corp.example") by Web.src Web.dest Web.user Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as url from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method="POST" Web.url="*ingest*sentry.io*envelope*" (Web.http_content_type="application/x-sentry-envelope" OR Web.http_user_agent!="sentry*") NOT Web.dest_domain IN ("sentry.your-corp.example") by Web.src Web.dest Web.user Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.
ATT&CKT1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry DeviceRegistryEvents
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\","\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\","\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0a
status: experimental
description: |
    Registry writes under the browser extension policy keys —
    administrative install of an extension. Often used by adware /
    info-stealers to bypass user-level extension controls.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1176/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1176
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    category: registry_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetObject|contains:
            - '\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Group-policy-managed extension whitelists
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

logsource:
    category: network_connection

detection:
    selection_ip:

     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]

10 year old critical vulnerability in phpBB affecting tens of millions of users across thousands of forums

Aikido
2026-06-10 5 use cases 2 techniques 4 kill-chain phases detected

Aikido Security discovered a critical unauthenticated authentication bypass in phpBB affecting tens of millions of users. A single HTTP request is all it takes to take over any account — a vulnerability that's been sitting in the codebase since 2014. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

Inventory of phpBB instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-29199 auth bypass AIReconnaissance High
Hunts the asset estate for phpBB installations on versions <= 3.3.16 or 4.0.0-a2 that are exposed to the OAuth authentication bypass and password-reset host-header injection chain. Output is a prioritized patch list, not a per-host alert. Rationale: Anchored on the article-named CVE-2026-29199 plus the two related CVEs (48611, 48612) surfaced via pentest-tools' research write-up that share the same patch (phpBB 3.3.17). Version-fallback regex catches assets where the CVE row hasn't yet propagated. Cross-checked: SentinelOne vuln DB (mechanism), phpBB.com release thread (patched-in-3.3.17 list), aikido article (affected versions string). Cross-checked against: • https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-29199/ • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170 • https://pentest-tools.com/research/phpbb-authentication-bypass • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/phpbb-forum-fixes-auth-bypass-bug-lurking-for-a-decade/

  • Test/staging phpBB instances intentionally pinned to 3.3.16 for upgrade rehearsal
  • Read-only forum archives queued for decommissioning where patching has been deferred
  • TVM scan lag — host has been patched but vuln record not yet retired (24-72h)
  • Third-party phpBB forks (e.g. phpBB3-SEO, custom MOD bundles) whose SoftwareName collides with stock phpBB but uses an independent version stream

| where not (MachineGroup has_any ("staging","dev","test","lab")) and not (DeviceName has_any ("-stg-","-dev-","-uat-"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: rank hits by IsInternetFacing == true, then by last seen LoggedOnUsers density (forum servers with admin sessions are tier-1). Confirm the live `<meta name="generator" content="phpBB 3.3.x">` tag with a quick curl. 2. Contain: for internet-facing critical hits, deploy the phpBB workaround thread's Host header allowlist in the web reverse proxy (forces `force_server_vars=1` behaviour) while planning the upgrade window; restrict OAuth endpoints at the WAF until 3.3.17 is in production. 3. Hunt: for each confirmed vulnerable host, pivot to UC2 (host-header injection on password reset) and UC3 (legacy OAuth endpoint hits) for the last 30 days to spot pre-patch exploitation.

phpBB password-reset Host header injection (CVE-2026-29199 core mechanism) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts inbound HTTP requests to phpBB's password-reset endpoints (ucp.php mode=sendpassword / confirm_reset_password) where the Host header does not match the site's canonical hostname — the exact pre-condition for the CVE-2026-29199 reset-link poisoning chain that yields account takeover on unpatched (<=3.3.16) installs. Rationale: Anchored on (1) the article's stated mechanism — a single unauthenticated request grants a session — and (2) SentinelOne's CVE-2026-29199 write-up identifying the bug as Host-header injection on the password-reset URL generator. The phpBB endpoint `ucp.php?mode=sendpassword` / `confirm_reset_password` is the literal handler. CanonicalHosts placeholder must be tuned per tenant — without that the rule fires on every reverse-proxy that doesn't normalise the Host header. No Sigma rule emitted because the detection is differential (host ≠ canonical), not a single-pattern match. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-29199/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/phpbb-authentication-bypass-rce • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672422
ATT&CKT1190 T1556 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal admin testing the password-reset flow from a jump host that hits the site via IP literal in the Host header
  • Health/uptime monitors (Pingdom, Datadog Synthetics) probing /ucp.php with their own Host header
  • Reverse proxy / CDN misconfiguration that injects 'localhost' or the upstream IP into the Host header before the app server logs it
  • Search engine bots crawling the password-reset page using the legacy bare-domain (no www) form before a 301 rewrite
Suppression filter
// Per-tenant: replace the CanonicalHosts dynamic literal with the real production hostnames; also exclude known monitoring IPs:
| where not (Source in ("203.0.113.10","198.51.100.20"))
| where not (UAs has_any ("Datadog/Synthetics","Pingdom","UptimeRobot"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the full request set for the suspect Source IP — does the SAME source hit the reset endpoint multiple times with DIFFERENT spoofed Host headers? That's exploitation. A single hit with one wrong Host is usually misconfig. Resolve the affected user (extract username from request body / response audit). 2. Contain: rotate the suspected victim's session and reset token via phpBB ACP, invalidate all active sessions for that account, and front the site with a WAF rule that drops password-reset POSTs whose Host header is not in the canonical allowlist. 3. Hunt: search the same source IP across UC3 (legacy OAuth endpoint hits) and SigninLogs/AAD activity for the victim account in the next 24h — successful logins from new IPs are the takeover confirmation.
let CanonicalHosts = dynamic(["forum.example.com","community.example.com"]);
let ResetHits_AppService = AppServiceHTTPLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where CsUriStem has "/ucp.php"
    | where CsUriQuery has_any ("mode=sendpassword","mode=confirm_reset_password")
    | extend HostHeader = tostring(CsHost), Source = tostring(CIp), Method = tostring(CsMethod), Status = toint(ScStatus)
    | project TimeGenerated, HostHeader, Source, Method, Status, CsUriStem, CsUriQuery, UserAgent, Referer, _ResourceId;
let ResetHits_WAF = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestURL has "/ucp.php" and RequestURL has_any ("mode=sendpassword","mode=confirm_reset_password")
    | extend HostHeader = tostring(DestinationHostName), Source = tostring(SourceIP), Method = tostring(RequestMethod), Status = toint(EventOutcome)
    | project TimeGenerated, HostHeader, Source, Method, Status, CsUriStem=RequestURL, CsUriQuery="", UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, Referer=RequestContext, _ResourceId;
union ResetHits_AppService, ResetHits_WAF
| where isnotempty(HostHeader)
| where not(HostHeader in~ (CanonicalHosts))
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), AnomalousHosts = make_set(HostHeader, 25), UAs = make_set(UserAgent, 10)
         by Source, Method
| order by LastSeen desc
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:azure.appservice OR source:iis) (@http.url_details.path:*/ucp.php* OR @http.url:*/ucp.php*) (@http.url:*mode=sendpassword* OR @http.url:*mode=confirm_reset_password*) -@http.host:(forum.example.com OR community.example.com)

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

phpBB legacy OAuth endpoint exploitation (post-3.3.17 patch window) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts HTTP requests to the legacy phpBB OAuth login and account-link URLs (ucp.php?mode=login&login=external&oauth_service=... and ucp.php?i=ucp_auth_link&...oauth_service=...) which were retired and replaced by /user/oauth/authenticate/... in phpBB 3.3.17. Continuing hits indicate unpatched instances and/or attacker probing of the CSRF/state-validation OAuth bypass. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim statement that the redirect URI handler 'is now located at /user/oauth/authenticate/...' — the OLD legacy URLs (ucp.php?mode=login&login=external&oauth_service= and ucp.php?i=ucp_auth_link&...) are documented on the phpBB.com 3.3.17 announcement thread. Per pentest-tools' research the CSRF/state-validation OAuth bypass (CVE-2026-48612) hinges on a missing `state` parameter check — the SPL/Sentinel queries surface that specifically via `HasState` flag. Defender/Falcon/CloudWatch left empty because none ship raw web access query strings by default. Cross-checked against: • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170 • https://pentest-tools.com/research/phpbb-authentication-bypass • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/phpbb-authentication-bypass-rce
ATT&CKT1190 T1078.004 T1550.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Forum still on 3.3.16 awaiting maintenance window — every legitimate OAuth login hits the legacy URL
  • OAuth provider (Google/Facebook) callback queued before the upgrade, replayed afterwards
  • Bookmarked legacy OAuth login URLs from registered users not yet redirected by 3.3.17's URL rewrite
  • Vulnerability scanners (Tenable, Qualys VM) probing both legacy and new OAuth endpoints
Suppression filter
// Suppress the unpatched-but-known crowd — once you've identified internal phpBB hosts still on 3.3.16, scope this rule to anomalous fan-out only:
| where DistinctSources > 5 or MissingStateCount > 0
// And exclude known scanners:
| where not (UAs has_any ("Qualys","Tenable","Nessus","Nuclei"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm target host version via the page generator meta tag or DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory join (link to UC1). If host is on 3.3.17+ then ANY legacy URL hit is suspicious — investigate the source IP for state-param absence (CVE-2026-48612 signature) and for fan-out across many user accounts. 2. Contain: if exploitation is confirmed, force-reset OAuth bindings for all users in `phpbb_user_group` table (ACP → User permissions → unlink external accounts), invalidate sessions, and rotate the OAuth client secrets at Google/Facebook/Microsoft provider side. 3. Hunt: search AAD/Google Workspace sign-in logs for the affected user pool — successful OAuth-token logins from new IPs in the 48h window post-exploit are the account takeover confirmation. Pivot the source IP across the last 30 days against UC2 to catch host-header injection attempts on the same campaign.
let LegacyOAuth_AppService = AppServiceHTTPLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where CsUriStem has "/ucp.php"
    | where CsUriQuery has_any ("login=external","ucp_auth_link","mode=auth_link")
    | where CsUriQuery has "oauth_service="
    | extend Source = tostring(CIp), Status = toint(ScStatus), HasState = CsUriQuery has "state="
    | project TimeGenerated, Source, CsHost, CsUriStem, CsUriQuery, Status, UserAgent, Referer, HasState, _ResourceId;
let LegacyOAuth_WAF = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestURL has "/ucp.php"
    | where RequestURL has_any ("login=external","ucp_auth_link","mode=auth_link")
    | where RequestURL has "oauth_service="
    | extend Source = tostring(SourceIP), Status = toint(EventOutcome), HasState = RequestURL has "state="
    | project TimeGenerated, Source, CsHost=DestinationHostName, CsUriStem=RequestURL, CsUriQuery="", Status, UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, Referer=RequestContext, HasState, _ResourceId;
union LegacyOAuth_AppService, LegacyOAuth_WAF
| summarize Hits = count(), MissingStateCount = countif(HasState == false), DistinctSources = dcount(Source), Statuses = make_set(Status, 10), UAs = make_set(UserAgent, 10), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Sources = make_set(Source, 25)
         by CsHost
| where MissingStateCount > 0 or DistinctSources > 5   // 5 = empirical pivot — legit OAuth callbacks come from the IdP not many client IPs
| order by LastSeen desc

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

| where Result =~ "success"

| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc
